newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI SOYBEAN FUTURES END UP ON SHORT-COVERING.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI SOYBEAN FUTURES END UP ON SHORT-COVERING.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Friday on short-covering after losses over the past few days, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,175 yuan ($383) per tonne, rising 25 yuan. It opened at a high of 3,180 yuan per tonne.
November rose 12 to 3,150, the January 1998 contract nine to 3,120 and March fell two to 3,116 per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 19,100 tonnes from 20,000 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly higher and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
"Short-covering was responsible for today's gains," one trader said.
"Many investors were eager to liquidate their short positions so they can move their money to other active markets including the stock market," he added.
Traders said they expected soybeans to rise slightly in the short term.
